tip: Set a weekly cap on food delivery orders. Delivery fees, platform charges and packaging make the same meal cost noticeably more than cooking or eating in.
Keep a few cheap, quick meals at home for busy days. Most delivery orders happen when nothing is ready to eat.
Check delivery apps for monthly passes or free-delivery thresholds, but only subscribe if you already order often enough to save.
Plan the week's groceries in one bigger shop and use a list. Many small quick-commerce orders add up through delivery and handling fees.
Buy staples like rice, dal and oil in bulk from a supermarket or local store, and keep quick delivery for emergencies.
Use a monthly bus or metro pass if you commute on most days. It is usually much cheaper than paying per ride.
Share rides or choose pooled options for regular routes, and save cabs for late-night or urgent trips.
Add items to the cart and wait 48 hours before paying. Many impulse purchases lose their appeal in that time.
Set a fixed monthly shopping budget and move the money into a separate account or UPI app when the month starts.
Before buying clothes or gadgets, check what you already own. Compare prices across two apps and ignore fake discount tags.
Review your subscriptions every month and cancel the ones you did not use. Rotate one streaming service at a time instead of paying for several.
Look for student offers and shared family plans for music and video services.
Set an entertainment limit per month for movies and events, and book weekday shows, which are often cheaper.
Compare mobile recharge plans once a year. A longer validity plan often costs less per month.
Turn off appliances you are not using. Even small changes can reduce an electricity bill over a few months.
Ask for generic medicines where your doctor agrees. They usually cost much less than branded ones.
Wait for sale periods on online courses and check whether your college or a free resource already covers the topic.
Write down who you lent money to and follow up. Untracked small transfers to friends quietly add up.
If rent is a big share of your budget, compare sharing options or locations that cut commute cost, since rent is your largest fixed cost.
Follow a simple split such as needs, wants and savings, and move your savings out as soon as money comes in, rather than saving what is left.
Review your top five merchants every month. Most overspending hides in a few repeat habits.
